hardinessNote: Tender, approximately 1 to 5°C (RHS 5036); a summer patio plant in most of the UK, or overwinter it frost-free.
foliage: evergreen; tiny narrow glossy dark green leaves on fine reddish stems
visual: Masses of tiny magenta-purple six-petalled flowers over a fine, heather-like mound of glossy little leaves · flowers summer into autumn
water: Keep evenly moist through summer, especially in pots; water sparingly over winter under cover.
soilWarning: Frost kills it; bring pots in before winter
prune: Trim lightly in spring to keep it bushy; pinch tips of young plants. No routine pruning needed.
resilience: Tough in heat and dry spells once settled; any frost kills top growth. Pests: whitefly, aphids and red spider mite under glass.
uses: Patio pots · bedding · edging · window boxes · conservatory · bees on the flowers
sources: RHS 5036, Cuphea hyssopifolia: H2, 0.1–0.5 m × 0.5–1 m in 5–10 years, compact bushy evergreen, full sun or partial shade, sheltered (search snippets)
Horticopia and US nurseries: USDA 8b–11, 30–60 cm × 30–90 cm, grown as an annual in colder areas
